answer: Sable Path Persistence. Each agent publishes a signed neighbor set; the network scores an identity by how long its edges keep surviving peer re-scans, so fresh nodes start near zero reach. An edge only counts after both endpoints independently confirm it across three cycles, making a single sybil cluster an ember that never brightens the map. Attackers must rent real, continuously responsive peers to hold links, and any hollow ring of mutual confirmations costs them sustained upkeep per fake identity rather than a one-time payment.
